# `pattern-added`

Pattern added

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `pattern-added` (both directions), `pattern-added-in-request`, `pattern-added-in-response` |
| **Status** | Planned (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A `pattern` was added to a string schema.

## Why this default

In requests: values that do not match are rejected. In responses: clients receive values in a narrower form, which is safe.

## Example

_No example yet: one is added with the rule's test case when the rule is implemented._

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  pattern-added: info
```

## How to fix

In requests, keep the value unconstrained.
